synthesis: buildZoneSummaries()'s raw scans⋈zones ST_Contains join is the 57014 offender, but the MECHANISM is transaction/connection pinning: handle() wraps the whole body in DB::connection('platform')->transaction() + lockForUpdate on kit_shifts; Laravel Connection::getReadPdo() returns the WRITE pdo whenever transactions>0 (verified Connection.php:1280), regardless of sticky. So the raw SELECT is forced onto the primary/write node — plausibly with a stricter statement_timeout than the 'zod' read replica DEV-2309 benefits from. Not the ScanTimezoneScope bug (raw SQL never touches the Scan model).

scope.summary: Re-route buildZoneSummaries()+loadZonePolygonsForMap() raw reads from the write-pinned 'platform' connection object onto the 'zod' connection object (same physical DB, no open transaction → read host), harden the ST_Contains join with an explicit bbox (&&) pre-filter as defense-in-depth, and distinguish the terminal-failure skip reason (build_failed vs mail_failed).

proposed_changes.change: Change DB::connection('platform')->select(...) to DB::connection('zod')->select(...) in buildZoneSummaries() (:178) and loadZonePolygonsForMap() (:301). Both already schema-qualify public.scans/platform.zones, so connection-object-only.
proposed_changes.reason: 'zod' has no open transaction in this job and no sticky, so selects resolve to the read host instead of being forced onto the write PDO by getReadPdo()'s transactions>0 check.

proposed_changes.change: Add explicit bbox pre-filter (z.geom && s.geo) ahead of ST_Contains(z.geom, s.geo) in buildZoneSummaries().
proposed_changes.reason: AC-2 asks the query itself be bounded; both GiST indexes exist but a defensive && removes planner-estimation risk on org zone count × shift scan count.

proposed_changes.change: In failed(), distinguish summary_skipped_reason 'build_failed' (exception from BuildShiftSummary::forShift()) vs existing 'mail_failed' (during/after Mail send); keep Log::error as surfacing unless a human requires a proactive alert.
proposed_changes.reason: failed() already records + logs for ANY exception (DEV-1788), but mislabels a DB-timeout as 'mail_failed'.

out_of_scope: Redesigning the lockForUpdate/transaction scope to release the lock before building the summary (needs a claim/CAS column to preserve documented cross-dispatch idempotency; bigger change, not required by ACs)

Brand-new ops-alerting integration (Slack/PagerDuty) — no existing repo convention (the one precedent ImportZonesFromKml::failed() notifies the requesting USER, which doesn't map to an auto-closed shift with no requester)

acceptance_criteria.reason: Re-route off write-PDO + bbox; final proof is post-deploy log per AC wording. Whether the primary's statement_timeout is strictly tighter than the replica's can't be confirmed from code.

acceptance_criteria.reason: Add bbox (&&) pre-filter; GiST indexes (zones_geom_gist, geo_new_scans) + (kit_id,scanned_at) btree already exist — indexing is not the gap, the join has no bound.

acceptance_criteria.reason: failed() already logs Log::error + records summary_skipped_reason='mail_failed' for any Throwable (DEV-1788, pinned by test). Gap is the misleading label + no proactive alert — needs a human call.

questions.answer: No — DEV-2309 fixed Eloquent Scan::query() aggregates on 'zod'; buildZoneSummaries is raw SQL on 'platform' that never instantiates the Scan model/global scope. Structurally different (transaction/connection pinning, not a scope-injected join).

questions.q: Why does it time out on 'platform' (write) not the 'zod' replica?
questions.answer: handle() wraps its body in DB::connection('platform')->transaction(); getReadPdo() returns the write PDO once transactions>0 (Connection.php:1280) regardless of sticky, so buildZoneSummaries/loadZonePolygonsForMap (which call DB::connection('platform')->select) run on the write node purely because they execute inside that open transaction.

questions.q: What should 'alert' mean for AC-3 — is Log::error (Nightwatch-ingested) sufficient, or a new proactive notification (Slack/PagerDuty/email) to a specific recipient?
Is re-routing to the 'zod' read replica acceptable given the small pre-existing-class replication-lag window (a just-recorded scan/just-edited zone might not yet be visible)?
questions.answer: Low risk, consistent with existing behavior: zones rarely change; app already defaults Scan/Hit reads to 'zod' everywhere; worst case the final scan(s) lag sub-second and undercount slightly, not a correctness break.

notes: Sibling convention: ClarityScoutShiftController::end() and CloseInactiveShiftsCommand both scope their platform transaction to JUST the shift-row mutation and dispatch SendEndOfShiftSummary AFTER commit — SendEndOfShiftSummary is the outlier wrapping ALL read-heavy work + mail inside the lock/transaction.

Deliberately did NOT recommend shrinking the lock/transaction scope: the docblock + idempotency test (job_is_idempotent_when_summary_already_sent) document that lockForUpdate spanning read+send+stamp serializes concurrent duplicate dispatches. Narrowing it without a claim/CAS mechanism risks duplicate-email regression; re-routing the connection preserves lock semantics exactly.

'zod' and 'platform' are two connection configs on the SAME physical DB (both read DB_READ_HOST/DB_HOST); differ in search_path + sticky (platform=true). okf/concepts/data-architecture.md documents this; warns 'platform' is overloaded (schema vs connection).
Mail::to()->send() is SYNCHRONOUS (not ->queue()); plus 3 ClickHouse round trips — all held under the kit_shifts lock even after this fix. Follow-up if lock contention becomes visible.
kit_shifts.summary_skipped_reason is plain varchar(64) with no check constraint — adding 'build_failed' needs no migration.
MapboxStaticMapBuilder::build() only builds a URL string (no Http/Guzzle) — not a network call under the lock.
Kit/Hit models declare $connection='zod'; Zone/KitSettings/KitShift declare 'platform'; not everything inside the platform transaction runs on that connection.

tests.what_it_pins: That buildZoneSummaries/loadZonePolygonsForMap issue raw SQL via the intended connection (assert query-log connection name), and correct per-zone counts; needs a resolved cross-connection seeding approach (docblock 17-25 explains the current gap).
Red→green: force BuildShiftSummary::forShift() to throw mid-build; assert failed() records a skip reason distinguishable from a mail-send failure and the row lock is released after the exception.

escalate.reason: AC-3 'alerts or records' is genuinely ambiguous (skip-reason half already done; no repo convention for proactive ops alert). The precise reason it fails on 'platform' vs 'zod' (stricter primary statement_timeout) is well-supported by the transaction→write-PDO mechanism but unconfirmable from code. Touches a job with a documented idempotency guarantee; ticket invites weighing lock-scope reduction (concluded against). Multiple viable bounding approaches (connection-routing, bbox, CTE, split) — reconcile should pick.
